title: Beaver Supermoon Lights Up the Sky Over Laredo
excerpt: November's full Beaver Supermoon shone over Laredo on Tuesday night, Nov. 24, 2026, two days before Thanksgiving, the first of three supermoons in a row.
content:
November's full moon, the Beaver Supermoon, shone bright over Laredo on Tuesday night, Nov. 24, 2026, two days before Thanksgiving.

The moon reached its full phase at 8:53 a.m. Central Time on Tuesday and appeared nearly fully illuminated through the night.

A supermoon looks larger and brighter than an average full moon because it is closer to Earth in its orbit.

The Beaver Moon takes its traditional name from the time of year when beavers prepare their shelters for the coming winter.

Tuesday's supermoon was the first of three in a row. The next, the Cold Moon, arrives Dec. 23, followed by the Wolf Moon on Jan. 22, 2027.
